cohort: Pregnant women at >34 weeks' gestation undergoing scheduled cesarean deliveries who experienced fetal bradycardia after spinal anesthesia and were converted to emergency cesarean delivery
finding: The rate of decrease in base excess when scheduled cesarean deliveries are converted to emergency cesarean deliveries owing to fetal bradycardia related to spinal anesthesia (1 mmol/2.6 min) matches the estimated rate of loss of base excess (1 mmol/2-3 minutes) reported in cases of severe bradycardia or sentinel events during labor.
mod_finding: This study examined fetal base excess decrease rates in scheduled cesarean deliveries converted to emergency procedures due to fetal bradycardia following spinal anesthesia.
birth_weight: Not below the 10th percentile for gestational age
